name: Critical
overview: Scripture teaches that being critical in speech and attitude requires careful restraint and humility. A gentle response can defuse anger, while harsh words provoke it, emphasizing the power of our communication (Proverbs 15:1). Believers are warned against judgmental attitudes, as judging others invites judgment upon oneself (Matthew 7:1), and are called to think soberly about themselves, recognizing the measure of faith God has given each (Romans 12:3). Speech should build up and minister grace, avoiding corrupt or harmful communication (Ephesians 4:29), while kindness, tenderheartedness, and forgiveness reflect the grace God has shown us in Christ (Ephesians 4:32). These truths underscore a Christ-centered approach to criticism that seeks restoration and love rather than condemnation.
